lesson.title: Social media, pupils’ photos and you
lesson.subtitle: Share the joy of the day, not the details of a child

video.title: Social media, pupils’ photos and you
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds; narration in the lesson language, captions as separate files.
cast: Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher (main character)
Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

chapters.label: Consent and what a photo says

scenes.visual: Sports day. Amina scrolls through photos on her phone: races, a trophy, smiling faces.
scenes.animation: Photos swipe past; she stops and frowns.
scenes.narration: Sports day was wonderful, and I took forty photos. I want to post the best ones on the school page tonight. But which ones? And who will see them?

scenes.visual: Title card with the Darsi mark and the course name.
scenes.on_screen_text: Social media, pupils’ photos and you
scenes.narration: Today: how to share pupils’ photos safely, and keep your own accounts professional.

scenes.visual: A signed consent form, a parent nodding, an older pupil asked with a question bubble.
scenes.animation: The form gets a tick; the bubble pops.
scenes.narration: Start with consent. Parents agree in writing, usually on the school’s consent form, before their child’s photo goes online. If a parent says no, that child isn’t in the photo. And older pupils deserve to be asked too.

scenes.visual: A photo of pupils with four details circled: a name caption, the school name on a jumper, a list on the board behind, a map pin hidden in the file.
scenes.animation: Circles draw around each detail as it is named.
scenes.narration: A photo can say more than you think. A full name under a face. The school’s name on a jumper, or on the gate. A list of names on the board behind. And the photo file itself may store where it was taken.

scenes.visual: A clean card with four rules and a camera icon.
scenes.animation: Rules tick in one by one.
scenes.narration: So here’s the rule. Post groups, or pupils from behind or far away. Never put full names next to faces. Check the background before you post. And turn off location tags in your camera.

scenes.visual: Four puzzle pieces: a uniform, a bus stop, a birthday cake, a pet. They click together into a map of a child’s day.
scenes.animation: Pieces slide together one by one.
scenes.narration: Small details add up, like pieces of a puzzle. A uniform, a bus stop, a birthday, a pet’s name. One piece tells a stranger nothing. Together, they tell them where a child will be, and when.

scenes.visual: Ms Salma holds up three sports-day photos as cards.
scenes.animation: Cards drop in with a small bounce.
scenes.narration: Quick check! Here are three sports-day photos. Which one is safest to post on the school page?

scenes.visual: The team-from-behind photo gets a check badge; the close-up slides into a family envelope.
scenes.animation: Check badge pops; the envelope closes.
scenes.on_screen_text: Share the joy, not the details
scenes.narration: The team from behind, with no names. You still share the joy of the day, but no stranger learns who, where or when. Send close-ups only to each child’s own family.

scenes.visual: Amina’s own profile: a lock, a declined friend request, the school’s official page, a search box with her name.
scenes.animation: Each item appears as it is said.
scenes.narration: Now your own accounts. Keep your personal profile private. Don’t accept pupils as friends on it. Talk to pupils and parents through the school’s official channels. And search your own name once a term, to see what others see.

scenes.visual: A fake school page post asking for fees to a new number, with red flags.
scenes.animation: Flags pop beside the post one by one.
scenes.narration: Sometimes a fake page pretends to be the school. It asks parents to pay next term’s fees to a new number, by Friday. Report the page to the platform. Then warn parents on the school’s official channel: the school never changes its payment number in a post.

scenes.visual: Six small post cards from a pupil; a magnifying glass joins them into one profile.
scenes.narration: In the lab, look at six harmless-looking posts by a pupil, and see what a stranger can piece together. Then make her profile safer.

scenes.visual: Amina’s phone shows a friend request from a pupil. Two answer cards bounce in.
scenes.animation: Cards bounce in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. A pupil sends you a friend request on your personal account. Accept it, or not?

scenes.animation: Cards line up left to right.
scenes.narration: Don’t accept: keep your personal and school accounts apart. Remember: consent first, groups with no names, check the background, and keep your own profile private.

scenes.visual: Amina’s classroom. Three photos drawn on the board; pupils circle details and suggest fixes.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: describe three photos, or draw them on the board. Pupils find every detail that gives away who, where or when, and suggest how to make each one safe to share.

checkpoints.prompt: Three sports-day photos. Which one is safest to post on the school page?

options.text: A close-up of the winner with her full name
The team from behind, with no names
The team at the school gate, with today’s date and time

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — it shares the joy, but no stranger learns who, where or when.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a name with a face, or the gate with the date and time, tell a stranger who, where and when. Post the team from behind, with no names.

checkpoints.prompt: A pupil sends you a friend request on your personal account. Accept it, or not?

options.text: Don’t accept — use the school’s official channels

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — keep personal and school accounts apart, and talk to pupils through official channels.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a personal account mixes your private life with your pupils’. Decline kindly and use the school’s channels.
